assumptions: The fluorescence falls as the duplex melts, so peaks of -dF/dT are melting transitions.
The expected Tm is the target product's, when the plate engine is to give verdicts.
limits: Only the plate engine gives verdicts; the vertex and curve engines report temperatures and areas.
Two products melting within a degree read as one peak.
bio.jane/contract.question: What is each reaction's melting temperature, and does its melt show the product, an artifact, or no amplification?

description: Melt curves to melting temperature, under any of THREE engines that answer different questions and none of which is a fallback for another. `plate` (RDML-Python) normalises, derives twice, calls the peaks of -dF/dT and CLASSIFIES them against the target's expected Tm into per-reaction verdicts — one peak in the window is the product, an extra peak is an artifact or a primer dimer, no peak at all is a reaction that did not amplify; it is the only engine that produces a verdict. `vertex` (MBmca diffQ) fits a quadratic near the extremum and reports its vertex, so the Tm is NOT one of the sampled temperatures — the only sub-grid answer. `curve` (qpcR) does no plate normalisation and gives no verdicts, but reports every melting peak with the AREA under it. Replicate spread travels with all three, because it describes the readings rather than the method.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

all_peaks.description: `vertex` only: report every peak the curve carries, not the dominant one alone. Only applies when engine is vertex. Advanced.

artifact_peak_width.description: `plate` only: half-width used when an extra peak is measured as an artifact. In C. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

bilin_high_start_temp.description: `plate` only: start of the high seed window. NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS, and upstream's own quirk reproduced: the high baseline scan walks a hard-coded 90-91 C seed, so this knob feeds ONLY the first exponential-free fit and moves the result far less than the low window does. The windows actually chosen come back in the result. In C. Only applies when norm_method is bilinear or combined. Advanced.

bilin_high_stop_temp.description: `plate` only: end of the high seed window — same narrow effect as its start, for the same reproduced reason. In C. Only applies when norm_method is bilinear or combined. Advanced.

bilin_low_start_temp.description: `plate` only: start of the LOW seed window the bilinear background is fitted from. In C. Only applies when norm_method is bilinear or combined. Advanced.

bilin_low_stop_temp.description: `plate` only: end of the low seed window. In C. Only applies when norm_method is bilinear or combined. Advanced.

cut_area.description: `curve` only: drop peaks whose area is under this fraction of the largest. 0 keeps every peak, which is upstream's own default. Only applies when engine is curve. Advanced.

engine.description: which of the three engines runs. They answer DIFFERENT questions: `plate` is the only one that produces a verdict, `vertex` the only one whose Tm is not a sampled temperature, `curve` the only one that reports peak areas. Values: plate (Plate (RDML-Python) - normalise, classify, verdicts), vertex (Vertex (MBmca diffQ) - sub-grid Tm), curve (Per curve (qpcR) - peak areas).

expected_tm.description: the product's expected melting temperature, which is what turns a peak list into a verdict. Left unset, every peak is reported and none is classified - an honest absence rather than a guess. Read by the `plate` engine only, because it is the only one that classifies. In C. Only applies when engine is plate.

expo_high_temp.description: `plate` only: high end of the exponential fit window. In C. Only applies when norm_method is exponential or combined. Advanced.

expo_low_temp.description: `plate` only: low end of the window the EXPONENTIAL background is fitted over. In C. Only applies when norm_method is exponential or combined. Advanced.

extremum.description: `vertex` only: which extremum the melt sits at. `auto` reads each curve's direction, because upstream assumes a signal that RISES with temperature and a solution-phase melt FALLS — on which the default walks to the far end of the curve and returns a plausible-looking wrong Tm. Only applies when engine is vertex.

fluor_source.description: `plate` only: which matrix a peak's fluorescence drop is read from — the normalised curve or the smoothed raw one. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

melt_table.description: the melt table: a header row, first column the temperature and every other column one reaction's fluorescence. The same table the Melt tab takes.

norm_method.description: `plate` only: how each curve is normalised before it is derived. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

peak_cutoff.description: `plate` only: the height a candidate must reach, as a percentage of the largest peak. In %. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

peak_high_temp.description: `plate` only: highest temperature a peak is looked for at. In C. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

peak_low_temp.description: `plate` only: lowest temperature a peak is looked for at. In C. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

peak_max_width.description: `plate` only: widest a peak may be before it is not read as one product. In C. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

replicate_percent.description: report replicate spread as a PERCENTAGE of the mean rather than in degrees. Advanced.

replicate_robust.description: replicate spread as median and MAD rather than mean and SD. Engine-independent: it describes the readings, so every run carries it. Advanced.

resample.description: `vertex` only: resample the curve onto an even temperature grid before differentiating. Only applies when engine is vertex. Advanced.

second_derivative.description: `vertex` only: locate the inflection points of the melt (diffQ2) rather than the peak of the first derivative. Only applies when engine is vertex. Advanced.

span_peaks.description: `curve` only: the span Friedman's super smoother uses when the peaks are called. Only applies when engine is curve. Advanced.

span_smooth.description: `curve` only: the smoothing span of the cubic spline fitted before the analytic derivative. Only applies when engine is curve. Advanced.

true_peak_width.description: `plate` only: half-width of the window around `expected_tm` a peak must fall in to count as the product. In C. Only applies when engine is plate. Advanced.

window_ceiling.description: `vertex` only: the largest neighbourhood half-width the quadratic is tried at. Every width from 2 up to this is fitted and the one with the best adjusted R-squared wins, so the Tm arrives with the fit quality that chose it. Only applies when engine is vertex.

name: analyze_melt_curves

classified.description: whether the peaks were classified, and why not when they were not — including 'this engine does not classify', which is a property of the choice and not a failure

derivativePlot.description: `plate` only: −dF/dT of each reaction after normalisation and smoothing, the curve its peaks are called on, one line per reaction. Null for `vertex` and `curve`, which fit near the extremum and report no whole derivative

engine.description: which engine produced these rows, named: the three answer different questions and a Tm without its engine is not comparable

meanTm.description: mean dominant Tm over the reactions that produced a peak

meltPlot.description: the melt curves as read from the table, one line per reaction, fluorescence against temperature. Every engine reads this same input

noPeak.description: reactions with no melting peak at all: a reaction that did not amplify, reported rather than dropped

reactions.description: one row per reaction, in the shape the CHOSEN engine reports: `plate` gives peaks plus a verdict, `vertex` gives the sub-grid Tm with the adjusted R-squared that chose its window, `curve` gives every peak with its area

replicateSpread.description: location and deviation per temperature per target, from the plate's own replicates. Engine-independent: it describes the readings, not the method, so every run carries it

targets.description: `plate` only: per target, the reactions that contributed a product peak and their averaged Tm against the expected one. Empty for `vertex` and `curve`
